title: 6 Months. 117 Shows. Here were my 6 favorites of the year (so far)! #...
transcript: We are officially halfway through 2026, which means it's time for my top six shows for the first six months before we start. Some honorable mentions because I'm not counting shows that I saw in previous years. So all of these shows I saw again this year and really loved, but won't be on this list. At number six, I have Animal Wisdom, which is one of those shows that I feel like is pushing the boundaries of what musical theatre as an art form can be. It is by Heather Christian, who I think is one of the most exciting musical theatre writers of today and, similar to a lot of her work, explores the idea of theatre as community, as spiritual, as ritual. And a show that I will be thinking about for a very long time. At number five, I have The Reservior a play by Jake Brasch starring Noah Galvin. I've now seen two of Jake's plays in addition to their work on American Sing Song, and they are quickly becoming one of my favourite up and coming playwrights. They are able to discuss such heavy and serious topics with a ton of levity and heart and humour. And some really great performances in this one as well. At number four, I have Ken Rex, which is essentially a one person true crime documentary. Jack Holden literally plays an entire town of people with such ease and the storytelling is gripping and tense and it was a story That I was not familiar with, so I was on the edge of my seat the entire time. At number three I have Black Swan, the only non New York production on this list. This is the kind of risky and bold musical theatre that I have been craving. It is a weird fever dream of a show, beautifully directed and choreographed by Sonya Tayeh and scored by Dave Malloy. It like 90% worked for me and if they could just fix that 10% we are going to have something very special on our hands. At number two I have birthright, which I actually just saw last night at the time of recording this. I'm going to do a full review on this one, but I really loved it. It is a three hour play dissecting the Jewish experience, but it absolutely flies by. I came out of that theatre and I was like, I could watch another three hours of that. And there are not that many shows that I feel that way about. This one is a must see, especially if you're Jewish. And finally my favorite show of the year so far. Cold War choir practice. Ironically also an MCC Show where birthright is currently playing. This is another show that is spanning so many different genres at once and yet totally works and feels so cohesive. The general vibe is a spy thriller told through the lens of a child who accidentally befriends a Russian agent. It was strange and off kilter, but I absolutely loved it.
